podcast_subtitle: The US insurance news briefing for agents and brokers.
podcast_description: An AI-generated ten-minute briefing on the US insurance market, every weekday morning. Rates and capacity, carrier appetite, claims and catastrophe losses, regulation, M&A and the insurtech deals that matter. Written for agents and brokers who need to know what moved before their first call of the day. Every episode is produced by AI from published trade press reporting, with sources named on air. AI can make mistakes - verify details before acting on them.
audience: independent US insurance agents and brokers - the people selling and servicing commercial and personal lines
editorial_brief: Pick what an agent or broker genuinely needs to know before their first call today. Strongly prefer: carrier appetite and capacity changes, rate movements, new products and programmes, carrier financial strength and solvency, catastrophe losses and claims trends, state regulation and compliance deadlines, agency M&A and consolidation, commission and compensation news, E&O exposure, and technology that changes how agencies actually operate. Downweight: individual crime and accident stories with no market implication, consumer-advice pieces, and vendor press releases with no substance. Prefer stories with a concrete consequence for someone placing business.

segments.label: Top story
segments.brief: A fixed AI disclaimer has just been read, so do not re-introduce the show or greet the listener again. Go straight into the single most consequential story of the day, name the date early in passing, and give a one-line tease of what else is coming. Fast.

segments.label: The rest of the day's news
segments.brief: Move briskly through the remaining stories, roughly a minute to ninety seconds each. Say what happened, name the source, and say what it means for an agency. Do not linger and do not pad.

segments.label: One thing worth understanding
segments.brief: Take one story and actually unpack it. The background a listener needs, what is genuinely at stake, who it helps and who it hurts, and what a broker should do about it. This is the segment that earns the subscription.

segments.label: Quick hits and sign-off
segments.brief: Rapid-fire remaining items - people moves, funding rounds, numbers worth knowing - a sentence each. Then a short sign-off. Mention the show returns tomorrow morning.

gemini_tts_style_prompt: A weekday morning news briefing for insurance professionals. Two American co-anchors who know this industry inside out and respect their listeners' time. Dana leads: crisp, warm, authoritative, the pace of someone with a lot to get through and no interest in wasting anyone's morning. Ray adds the context and the occasional dry aside. Both speak in natural American accents, clearly and briskly, but like people talking rather than reading. Emphasis on the numbers and the names that matter. Confident, awake, unhurried enough to be understood. Never breathless, never a hard-sell radio voice, never flat.
disclaimer_text: First, a quick note on what this is. Insurance Daily is an AI-generated briefing. Every weekday morning we scan the industry trade press, pick out the stories that matter most to agents and brokers, and turn them into this show. The voices you are hearing are synthetic, and the script is written by AI from published reporting. We name our sources as we go so you can check them. But AI can and does get things wrong, so please treat this as a starting point and not as a source of record. Verify the detail before you act on anything you hear here.
show_notes_disclosure: This podcast is generated by AI from published trade press reporting. Sources are named in the episode. AI can make mistakes - please verify any detail before acting on it.
